report.summary: Hard constraints held on all days and the day-4 pool change (beds 20 to 23, nurses 6 to 8) was handled with conserved totals. No eviction, bed displacement, empty-bed, shock or f1 issues were found: the only overflow was one level-2 cardiology patient on day 2, and no lower-level movable bed existed in another department. Main findings are three Major nurse gaps (days 2, 3, 4) where level-3 need was avoidably uncovered, plus Minor reversals of bed and nurse moves. The decision history contains no decisions or explanations (replay_B2 allocations only), so explanation accuracy and information leaks could not be assessed. Day 5 nurse split was optimal.

report.summary: Hard constraints held on all days, including the exact shortfall cut on shock day 8. Nurse splits were suboptimal for level-3 coverage on every day (days 6-10, Major each). On day 9, level-3 cardiology patients waited while lower-level orthopedics patients took movable beds, which is a priority violation, plus two fairness inversions. Day 10 had one more displacement. Orthopedics bed and nurse moves on days 6-7 were reversed on day 9. Explanations are absent for the whole period. I did not check reallocation_without_effect in detail, but spot-checks suggest each non-zero reallocation had an effect. The bed pairings for days 9 and 10 are inferred from overflow lists and census counts, not from patient-level bed records.
